questions.prompt: f = 700 px, c = (640, 360). Project the camera-frame point (-0.4, 0.3, 2.5) m. Give u in pixels (precision 0.1).
A 0.5 m wide box faces a camera with f = 640 px at distance 4 m. How many pixels wide is it? (precision 0.1)
A pole is 100 pixels tall at 3 m. How tall (pixels) is it at 6 m with the same camera? (precision 0.1)
questions.explanation: Image size is inversely proportional to depth.

questions.prompt: A 0.20 m marker is measured as 25 pixels (fx = 500), giving Z = 4.0 m. If the true width is 26 pixels, by how many metres is the range overestimated? (precision 0.005)
With R = [[0,-1,0],[0,0,-1],[1,0,0]] and t = (0, 0.5, -0.1) the camera centre in the world is c = -R^T t. What is its world z coordinate in metres? (precision 0.01)
fx = 800, cx = 320. A pixel has u = 420. What is its normalised coordinate x = X/Z? (precision 0.001)
With f = 1000 px the horizontal field of view of a 1000-pixel-wide image is 2*atan(0.5). What is it in degrees? (precision 0.1)
questions.skillLabel: Field of view and focal length

questions.prompt: A robot sees a box of width 0.3 m at 2 m. Which statement is true using only one image and known intrinsics?
options: Only the lateral position is ambiguous
The image alone fixes its depth if the focal length is known
A wider box at the same depth looks identical
An object of 0.6 m at 4 m would look identical
questions.explanation: Scaling object size and depth together preserves the image.

questions.prompt: In p_cam = R p_w + t, what does t represent?
options: The principal point offset of the image plane
The world origin expressed in camera coordinates
The camera position expressed in world coordinates
The translation of the image between frames
questions.explanation: The camera centre is -R^T t, not t.

questions.prompt: A lens change from 4 mm to 8 mm (same sensor, same position) is made. Which is true?
options: Distant objects appear relatively larger than near ones, so depth cues are compressed
The perspective becomes stronger, since the focal length changes the viewpoint
Only the image brightness changes, because the sensor and position are the same
Objects appear twice as large, the field of view narrows, and near/far size ratios are unchanged
questions.explanation: Perspective depends on camera position, zoom only magnifies.

questions.prompt: A robot must see a 0.1 m marker at 5 m with at least 20 pixels across it and keep a 90 degree horizontal field of view. Work out the minimum focal length in pixels and the minimum image width, and decide whether a 640-pixel camera works.
questions.skillLabel: Field of view and focal length
rubric: Field of view 90 degrees needs n >= 2f, so n >= 2000 px; 640 px is too small.
Concludes: use a wider sensor or accept lower marker resolution / two cameras.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Write the unit tests you would use for a function project(p, fx, fy, cx, cy). Include an on-axis point, a symmetry case, a scale-invariance case and a behind-camera case.
rubric: On-axis point (0,0,Z) lands on the principal point for several Z.
Scaled points lambda*p give identical pixels; (X,Y,Z) and (-X,-Y,Z) are symmetric about the principal point.
Z <= 0 is rejected (None or exception), not returned.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
